item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Nitin must report how many chairs to buy for $47$ guests when chairs are sold only in packs of $10$. He also has a separate tally that must record the exact guest count.

Which claim fits each need?

options.A: Call both answers "approximate value" only, without choosing exact, round-up, round-down, or nearest-place for each need.
options.B: Say that writing a rounded chair count is what creates the exact guest tally of $47$, instead of keeping the tally exact because that need requires exactness.
options.C: Buy $50$ chairs (round up in packs of $10$ so every guest has a seat) and keep $47$ exact in the guest tally.
options.D: Decide only by asking whether $47$ feels "big" or "small" in everyday talk, without using exact versus round-up/round-down/nearest-place for these two needs.
